text:
erin: quick question — enterprise customer asked that tenant admins shouldn't see per-route routing policies (they find it confusing). do we hide the routing controls entirely or show a simplified surface?

mohit: +1 on simplifying. routing policies expose a lot of infra knobs (priority, fallback-models, region-affinity). tenant admins usually only need 'route -> quota' and 'enable/disable'. :thinking:

lena: my worry is that hiding them removes important controls for platform teams that operate as tenant admins. we should make them discoverable behind 'advanced' not disabled.

priya: proposal: two-tier view — basic (toggle, quota slider, SLA label) and advanced (full policy editor JSON + rollout controls). default to basic for tenant-admin role.

erin: how do we map with our RBAC scopes? currently roles: org-admin, tenant-admin, support. We can add scope:routing. if tenant-admin lacks routing scope they see basic only.

mohit: will require API change. GET /console/v1/tenants/:id/ui-config?scopes=... to return feature flags. small change but needs migration for Dedicated/Private.

lena: related: telemetry — if we hide policy fields in UI, we still need to show telemetry for the route (latency, cost, fallback rate). ops will complain if they lose visibility. we must keep telemetry panels for all roles with read-only view.

priya: agree. read-only telemetry + admin-only editing. also audit logs must record who toggled fallback/rollout. add explicit audit event for 'route.policy.edit'.

mohit: implementation detail: UI uses a per-route permission check we already have for 'edit_route'. add `edit_route.policy` granular check. console will fetch permissions via /auth/v1/effective-perms which already returns list of allowed actions.

erin: can we avoid a breaking change for Private installs? prefer feature-gated approach: if backend doesn't return granular perms, fall back to showing full policy (old behavior). add a console warning: 'Permissions granularity unavailable for this deployment'.

lena: rollout UX — we should surface canary config in advanced editor with safe defaults (10% traffic, 1 hour). and a simple 'promote' button in basic that surfaces a modal with two bullets: canary% and duration.

priya: telemetry privacy: some customers want to redact model metadata in the telemetry for legal reasons. we should add a per-tenant flag `telemetry_model_visibility: full|redacted|none`. default full.

mohit: that ties into ingestion pipeline. redaction should happen upstream before metrics are sent to the console backend. add a note to migrations doc.

erin: sounds like next steps: 1) design basic/advanced mocks for route editor 2) add `edit_route.policy` to auth service + fallback behavior 3) telemetry read-only panel for tenant-admins + redaction flag + audit events 4) document Private migration path. I'll draft RFC.

deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: ui/route-editor v2 -> canary (5% users) at 2024-05-12T14:00Z :eyes:

lena: thanks — i'll start the mocks and tag priya for copy.

priya: will write audit requirements and canary defaults.

erin: great, tagging product to review the defaults tomorrow. :+1:
